title: Asymmetric padding: memory-bank usage and occupancy notes
body:
Summary:
Quick notes from an exploratory sweep on asymmetric input padding and how it affects memory bank contention and SM occupancy for our decoder microbatches. Motivation came from odd tail-latency spikes when mixing very short and long sequences in the same microbatch — not explained by batching alone. Hypothesis: asymmetric padding causes strided accesses in shared memory / L2 that amplify bank conflicts for the attention kernel and can reduce effective occupancy due to replay/backoff in some kernels.

Experiment setup:
- Model: distilled-3B baseline build used in canary (fp16).
- HW: A100 40GB, CUDA 11.8, driver 525.x, nsight compute v2024.3 snapshot.
- Workloads: controlled microbatches (B=4,8) with input length mixes: 
  * uniform-short (all 32)
  * uniform-long (all 1024)
  * mixed-asymmetric (3 x 32, 1 x 1024)
  * interleaved (32,1024,32,1024)
- Padding strategy: naive right-pad to max within batch vs group-wise padding (2 groups: short/long).
- Instrumentation: nvprof->nsight compute captures for attention kernel; NVTX ranges around batch prep and KV cache warmup; L2/sharedmem counters, bank_conflict counter, achieved_occupancy and active_warps.

Key observations:
- Mixed-asymmetric (naive pad) shows 15–25% lower achieved_occupancy on the attention kernel vs uniform-long, despite identical theoretical concurrency (same microbatch). Active warp counts fluctuate with large idle periods seen in SM timeline.
- Bank conflict counter increases 3x for mixed-asymmetric compared to uniform-long on sharedmem reads inside softmax/attention matmul epilog. Trace shows repeated serialization in some warps (lane divergence pattern).
- NVLink/host copy not implicated — this is purely GPU internal pattern.
- Group-wise padding (two sub-batches) recovers most occupancy and reduces bank conflicts; tail latency 90p improves ~18%.
- Interleaved ordering (alternating short/long) is worst for occupancy — suggests layout and coalescing are sensitive to contiguous tile ordering.

Preliminary root causes (working hypotheses):
1) Asymmetric padding creates irregular memory stride for per-token softmax accumulators and KV writebacks — when short sequences are right-padded, some threads do no-ops but still participate in memory writes, leading to imbalanced bank use.
2) The decoder's epilogue path triggers divergence on lane masks for padding lanes which then generates nondeterministic memory access ordering that serializes bank accesses on SM.
3) CUDA graph replay interacts poorly with the above pattern when kernels are fused, magnifying the observed SM idle pockets (observed in timeline snapshots).

Immediate mitigations tested (cheap, no model change):
- Reorder microbatch to colocate similar-length sequences (grouping) — easy in batcher and shows large wins.
- Apply group-wise padding at Batcher level (sub-batch padding) — adds a small scheduling complexity but good tradeoff.
- Add quick NVTX markers and a guard in attention kernel that bypasses the epilogue for fully-padded lanes (avoid writes). This reduces bank_conflict counter by ~30% in synthetic trace (needs careful correctness check).

Open questions / next steps:
- Need to validate across other GPUs (H100) and quantized kernels (int8 path) — does quantization change alignment/bank pressure?
- Is there an opportunity to modify kernel tile layout (transpose vs contiguous) to smooth bank usage without extra branching? Could be a small kernel redesign.
- Test with CUDA graph captured paths vs non-captured dynamic dispatch — we saw different SM idle patterns. Capture variant seems to amplify streaks; need a dedicated replay/no-replay A/B test.
- Add a lightweight per-batch analyzer in the router to recommend grouping when variance of lengths > threshold. Rough sketch: if len_stddev/len_mean > 0.6 then attempt group-split.

Action items:
- Priya: run same workload on H100 and post raw nsight captures (JIRA RI-8421) — due 2026-02-09.
- Marta: prototype guard in attention epilogue to skip writes on padded lanes, create small perf PR against canary nightly image. Link PR in linked_artifacts.
- Evan: implement batcher-side group-wise padding experiment in staging traffic, measure 90/95 tails for mixed production traces.
- Liam (me): follow-up timeline captures focusing on CUDA graph vs direct launch (two runs, identical dispatch order) and collect SM idle histograms.

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Keep an eye on L2 miss rate change when switching to group-padding — could move pressure to L2 if many long sequences batched together.
- Consider adding a small microbenchmark that reproduces padding-bank conflict without full model (tiny kernel that mimics epilogue writes) — will speed iteration.
- Link to related bucket: CONFLUENCE-occupancy-wg has prior notes on bank thrashing but this asymmetric-padding angle is new.

References and quick links: CONFLUENCE-occupancy-wg, JIRA-RI-8421, PR 367 in serving-runtime repo.

Unresolved: exact mapping between warp-lane masks and bank indexing for our runtime memory layout. Might be driver/hardware dependent — reach out to SRE infra team if we need vendor guidance.

End of notes (working doc).
